svg.text: DC-COUPLED MINI-GRID — REPRESENTATIVE SINGLE LINE DIAGRAM
Typical African village system: ~15 kWp PV · ~60 kWh battery · 20 kVA genset · 400/230 V LV network
Owner: site owner · ~15 kWp, fixed tilt
Fuel tank, level sensor and bunded slab
DC surge arresters and fuses on every string and pole
Earth mat, bonding and lightning air terminals
Battery room ventilation, temperature and gas alarm
Earth-fault protection and RCDs on customer feeders
Fire detection and extinguishers in the powerhouse
All solar passes through the battery bus, so one conversion step is saved on the charging path.
The inverter–charger is the only route to the loads: it is the single point of failure of this topology.
The genset feeds the inverter AC input, so it cannot supply the village unless a bypass is fitted.
Battery voltage sets the DC bus voltage, so string design, cable size and volt-drop must be checked.
Best suited below roughly 15–20 kW and where most demand is in the evening.
Ratings, cable sizes and protection settings follow the national LV code and the site load study.
